licence.title: Physician Assistant license (PA-C)
licence.renewalDeadline: October 31 of the renewal year (online renewal September 1 to October 31); 100% late fee after expiry

ce.hoursNote: No Montana CME requirement for PA renewal was found; the former rule requiring PAs to maintain NCCPA certification (ARM 24.156.1616) was repealed effective April 29, 2017. NCCPA exam passage is a licensure criterion only.
ce.controlledSubstanceCe: None found in Montana PA statute or rules.

practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: Only PAs with fewer than 8,000 hours of postgraduate clinical experience need a collaborative agreement (with a physician or a PA who has 8,000 or more hours), documented in written practice-level policies and procedures that are provided to the Board on request; not routinely filed. PAs who actively practised 8,000 hours before October 1, 2023 are exempt.
practice.notes: Chart review frequency and amount are set at the practice level in the collaboration agreement (ARM 24.156.1623). PAs who qualify for independent practice (8,000 hours) apply for an Independent Practice endorsement on the licence through the Board (Board instructions). Montana participates in the PA Licensure Compact (ARM 24.156.1627, effective May 9, 2026).

prescribing.stateCsRegistrationNote: Statute requires DEA registration for PAs who prescribe controlled substances (MCA 37-20-404(3)(d)). Every Title 37 prescriber must register with the Montana Prescription Drug Registry at initial licensure or renewal (MCA 37-7-1503), pays an annual registry fee (MCA 37-7-1511) and must check the registry before prescribing an opioid or benzodiazepine (MCA 37-7-1515). Whether the Board of Pharmacy requires a separate state controlled substance registration for prescribers (MCA 50-32-301 and 50-32-308 speak of registration of dispensers and practitioners) was not confirmed.
prescribing.separateAuthorityNote: Prescribing authority is statutory: Schedules III to V, Schedule II limited to periods not exceeding 34 days.

aprn.title: APRN license (Certified Nurse Practitioner, CNP)
aprn.renewalDeadline: December 31 (odd or even year by licensee); APRN page and prescriptive authority page differ on whether all nursing licences renew in even years
aprn.ceNote: The former 24 contact hours (12 pharmacology for prescribers) were repealed in 2023. APRN must submit verification of national recertification within 30 days of issuance and keep an individualized quality assurance plan.

prescribing.separateAuthorityNote: Prescriptive authority endorsement on the APRN licence (ARM 24.159.1463), renewed concurrently with the licence every two years; lapses 45 days after a missed renewal and then requires reapplication.
prescribing.pharmacologyCeForPrescribers: None per cycle. Initial endorsement: graduate pharmacology course within 5 years, or a 3 credit course or 45 contact hours of pharmacology CE if graduated more than 5 years ago.
prescribing.stateCsNote: No Board of Nursing controlled substance registration beyond the prescriptive authority endorsement. Every Title 37 prescriber registers with the Montana Prescription Drug Registry at initial licensure or renewal (MCA 37-7-1503), pays an annual registry fee (MCA 37-7-1511) and checks the registry before prescribing an opioid or benzodiazepine (MCA 37-7-1515). A separate Board of Pharmacy controlled substance registration for prescribers (MCA 50-32-301, 50-32-308) was not confirmed either way.

practice.authorityNote: Label follows the AANP taxonomy; primary rule describes APRN practice as independent and/or collaborative with no physician agreement requirement found in ARM 24.159.14.

MT NP: renewal year conflict. The APRN and RN pages say odd or even licensees renew December 31 of their year; the Prescriptive Authority page says all nursing licences renew December 31 of even years. ARM 24.101.413 says only 'Biennially, December 31'. Take the year from the licence itself.
